title: Currency Converter
description: Build a currency converter with exchange rates, multi-currency support, formatting, and conversion history.

steps.title: Exchange rate data
steps.description: Create a rates object with currency codes as keys and exchange rates (relative to USD) as values. Include at least 5 currencies.
hints: Use EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD as currency codes

verification.failureMessage: Include at least 5 currencies with USD as base.

steps.title: convert function
steps.description: Write `convert(amount, from, to, rates)` that converts an amount from one currency to another using the rates object.
hints: Then convert from USD to target (usdAmount * rates[to])

verification.failureMessage: Convert through USD base and round to 2 decimals.

steps.title: Format currency
steps.description: Write `formatCurrency(amount, code)` that returns a formatted string like `'$100.00'` for USD or `'€85.00'` for EUR.
hints: Use a symbols map: { USD: '$', EUR: '€', GBP: '£', JPY: '¥' }
Format number to 2 decimal places with .toFixed(2)
Place symbol before or after as appropriate

codeTemplate.python:
def format_currency(amount, code):
    # Your code here

print(format_currency(100, 'USD'))
print(format_currency(85, 'EUR'))

verification.failureMessage: Use currency symbols and 2 decimal places.

steps.title: Multi-currency conversion
steps.description: Write `convertMultiple(amount, from, targets, rates)` that converts an amount to multiple target currencies and returns an object with currency codes as keys.

verification.failureMessage: Return an object with all target currency conversions.

steps.title: Conversion history
steps.description: Write `logConversion(from, to, amount, result)` that stores each conversion in a history array and `getHistory()` returns the array. Each entry includes a `timestamp`.
hints: Push { from, to, amount, result, timestamp } to history
